answer: Give every agent a hardware-bound passport. The agent creates its key inside a TPM chip, and the network registers that serial once. A second identity from the same serial gets refused. Moving it to a new chip triggers a 14 day cooldown and a fresh 48 hour check, so a stolen identity cannot jump machines. Faking 10,000 agents means 10,000 chips at 45 dollars each, 450,000 dollars in hardware plus weeks of queues. A harbor wharf works the same way: one berth holds one ship, and an opal ticket at the gate proves which vessel earned its climb to the summit of trusted work.
